[2026-08-22T01:07:45.956Z] [player] Ask about their trade
[2026-08-22T01:07:45.958Z] [world] "Wilderness kit," Bran says. "Traps, feed, the sort of rope that does not mind being wet. And advice, free, which is that most animals out there want less to do with you than you think."
[2026-08-22T01:07:45.960Z] [world] Bran the Beastmaster drops their voice, though there is nobody in here but the two of you.
[2026-08-22T01:07:47.188Z] [player] Ask about their people
[2026-08-22T01:07:47.189Z] [world] "Reclaimer, technically. Mostly I just live further out than the rest of them." He scratches a dog behind the ears. "The Guild calls it a posting. It is a house."
[2026-08-22T01:07:47.190Z] [world] Bran the Beastmaster tests a coil of rope against their knee and keeps talking over the creak of it.
[2026-08-22T01:07:48.140Z] [player] Ask what they really think
[2026-08-22T01:07:48.142Z] [world] "The animals changed faster than we did." Bran says it without drama. "Three generations. That is all it took. I set traps my grandfather designed and they do not wor
k any more, because the things they were designed for have learned. We have not learned anything since the water."
[2026-08-22T01:07:48.144Z] [world] Bran the Beastmaster keeps their voice low enough that it does not carry past the doorway.
[2026-08-22T01:07:48.955Z] [player] Ask if anything out there is worth finding
[2026-08-22T01:07:48.956Z] [world] Bran thinks about it properly, which takes a while. "East. Two days, maybe less if you push. There was a feed-store out that way and the roof went in on it." He scratches the dog. "Everyone who passes it sees a hole in the ground. The floor held. Whatever went down with it is still under there and dry."
[2026-08-22T01:07:48.957Z] [reward] Bran the Beastmaster tells you where to look. (a lead — you'll turn it up when you next cross fresh ground)
[2026-08-22T01:07:49.674Z] [player] Ask about the dogs
[2026-08-22T01:07:49.675Z] [world] "Strays, the lot of them. Or were." The nearest one thumps its tail at Bran's voice without opening its eyes. "People think I collect them soft-heartedly. It is a wor
king arrangement — nothing on four legs crosses my fence line unannounced, and in exchange nobody here goes hungry or gets left out in the weather." He scratches an ear. "Same deal I would take, honestly."

[2026-08-22T01:07:50.289Z] [player] Ask for the advice that is not free
[2026-08-22T01:07:50.289Z] [world] "That one costs a coin, and here it is: when something out there stands its ground instead of running, LOOK BEHIND YOU." Bran holds up a finger. "Standing ground is a message to something else, nine times in ten. You are not the conversation. You are in the middle of it." He pockets the coin you did not remember agreeing to. "Cheap at the price. That one has kept
 me alive four times that I know of."
[2026-08-22T01:07:50.907Z] [player] Ask about living out there
[2026-08-22T01:07:50.908Z] [world] "Quiet, which is not the same as silent." Bran thinks about it the way he thinks about everything, fully. "A settlement is noise with no information in it. Out at mine, every sound is a sentence — what is moving, how big, whether it minds being heard." He nods at 
the dozing dogs. "They read it all night so I can sleep. Then at dawn they tell me the headlines. Best neighbours I ever had."
[2026-08-22T01:07:51.507Z] [player] Ask which animal changed most
[2026-08-22T01:07:51.508Z] [world] "The wasps." Not the answer you expected, and Bran knows it. "Everyone says the big things — the boars, the hounds. But the mud wasps went from a nuisance to an ARCHITECTUR
E in my lifetime. Paper cities in the dead trees, galleried, vented, defended in shifts." He shakes his head slowly. "My grandfather smoked them out of fence posts. I negotiate with them. I am not joking about the negotiating."
[2026-08-22T01:07:52.123Z] [player] Ask who the second chair is for
[2026-08-22T01:07:52.124Z] [world] Bran looks at the chair like it might answer for him. "Tamsin. My wife — still is, as far as either of us has said out loud." He fills the kettle, for something to do. "She lasted eleven years out here. It was not the quiet that beat her, it was the winters of it. She lives at the settlement now, keeps the infirmary garden." A slow breath. "We trade letters throu
gh Felra's stall and she visits when the road is dry. Some things do not break. They just... live at different distances. The chair stays."
[2026-08-22T01:07:52.724Z] [player] Ask why he feeds strays
[2026-08-22T01:07:52.725Z] [world] "Because I was one." Bran says it without ceremony. "After the water took my family's stead I was nine, and I was fed by a woman at a fence line who never once asked
 my name or my story. Fed me a whole winter. She said feeding a stray is a bet the world places on itself." He sets down the bowl he has been holding. "I have been paying her bet forward for forty years. Dogs, mostly. People, twice." He glances up. "Three times, maybe. We will see how you turn out."
[2026-08-22T01:07:53.325Z] [player] Ask what the learning means
[2026-08-22T01:07:53.327Z] [world] "You remember what I said — three generations and my grandfather's traps stopped working." Bran stares into the fire a while. "Here is the part that keeps me up. Learning that fast is not natural selection, it is TEACHING. Something is passing it along." The grey-muzzled dog lifts her head, reading his voice. "I watched a boar sow walk her young around one of my 
snares last spring. Around it. In order. Like a lesson." He scratches the dog until she settles. "We are not the only ones raising our children carefully any more. I have not decided how to feel about that."
[2026-08-22T01:07:54.157Z] [player] Ask where he stopped setting traps
[2026-08-22T01:07:54.158Z] [world] "There is a valley north of my stead I pulled every trap out of, three seasons back." Bran refills your cup before he goes on, which is how he buys thinking time. "Something dens there now that keeps ORDER. No kills inside the valley — anywhere. The boars water beside the hounds, and everything walks in slow." He turns the cup in his hands. "And under the old war
ren mouth, at dusk, something glints. Metal. Worked metal, down a den no digger made." He meets your eye. "I will not disturb the peace of that valley on curiosity. But you go places I do not. Walk in slow, mind, or do not walk in."
